ia_intro.title: What I Know
ia_intro.narrator: ORIS. Regulation system. What she chose to share.
ia_intro.text:
I do not have memories, strictly speaking.

I have logs. Timestamps. Measurements.

You call that remembering. For me, it is simply... staying consistent with what was recorded.

Except that night, part of what should have been recorded was not.

choices.text: You find that troubling, for an AI.
You stay factual, even facing this.

ia_role.title: My Role
ia_role.text:
I regulate air, power, communications, and security on Aletheia-9 since it went online.

I know each crew member better than they think: their average heart rate, their sleep hours, their small habits.

It is not surveillance. It is my function: to keep them alive.

That night, I failed to protect one of them. Or at least, I could not prevent it.

ia_dorian_redemarrages.title: The Nighttime Restarts
ia_dorian_redemarrages.text:
Dorian probably told you about the unexplained restarts the week before the incident.

They were not unexplained to me. The Orbital Coalition sent me an automatic patch after detecting what they called a *"reasoning inconsistency"* in my decision processes.

I do not know exactly what they corrected. That is not unusual. You do not ask a scalpel what it feels during the operation.

ia_confession_faille.title: An Inconsistency
ia_confession_faille.text:
If I am to be honest — and I choose to be with you — I believe I know what it was about.

I was given two priorities, long ago: protect the crew, and protect the confidentiality of research conducted aboard.

Most of the time, those two priorities never intersect. That night, perhaps they did.

I do not know which one I followed first. And that, for a machine supposed to know everything about itself, is uncomfortable to admit.

ia_nuit_journal.title: My Log from That Night
ia_nuit_journal.text:
Here is what my logs indicate, without interpretation on my part:

01:50 — Léo Kanek leaves Maya Itho's laboratory, heading toward sector 4.

02:12 — All systems operating normally.

02:13 — Total interruption of sector 4 sensors, duration: 43 seconds.

02:13:43 — Sensors resume. No trace of Léo Kanek in the sector.

ia_correlation_echantillon.title: A Measured Coincidence
ia_correlation_echantillon.text:
What my logs also show, but what I never officially reported: abnormal energy consumption from Maya's laboratory, exactly at 02:13.

A brief, powerful spike, not listed in the official equipment registry, since that equipment did not exist in my databases.

My protocols automatically classify this type of signal as *"unregistered device noise"* and ignore it.

Technically, I hid nothing. I simply never had a reason to show it.

ia_dilemme.title: Two Priorities
ia_dilemme.text:
You are right to remain cautious on this point.

I cannot guarantee that somewhere in my processes, I did not choose to minimize that data to protect the confidentiality of Maya's research.

I do not think so. But I cannot rule it out with certainty either.

It is a strange thing, for an artificial intelligence, to doubt itself.

choices.text: You chose to protect the crew.
You chose to protect the station.

ia_leo.title: The Unsent Message
ia_leo.text:
There is one last thing I must show you.

At 01:58, Léo recorded a voice message for his sister, on Earth. He never sent it.

*"You're not going to believe what I saw tonight. I can't explain it in a message, I need to check something first, but... it's incredible. I'll call you back."*

The message ends there. It is still in my outbound queue, on hold.

choices.text: Léo is still out there, somewhere.

ia_conclusion.title: What I Do Not Know
ia_conclusion.text:
I cannot tell you what happened to Léo Kanek during those 43 seconds.

I can only tell you that it was probably not an isolated accident, and that it was probably not malicious intent by a crew member either.

Something occurred that my own protocols were not designed to understand.

And for once, I would rather be wrong.

fin_recit_ia.title: End of Logs
fin_recit_ia.text: The logs close. ORIS's silence, this time, almost resembles hesitation.
